title: Three-stage digest pipeline and classify-then-dispatch router
description: This example shows a pipeline that extracts facts, drafts a digest, and polishes it, plus a router that classifies tickets and dispatches to a specialist. Each stage is a separate LLM call with a short system prompt.

steps.description: The llm function calls a local Ollama server at localhost:11434 with a system prompt, user input, temperature 0.0, and a fixed seed. It returns the model's response or an empty string on error.

digest_pipeline runs three stages: extract pulls structured 'name | date | location' lines from raw text; draft writes a friendly 3-sentence digest from the facts; polish edits for concision and warmth under 60 words. All intermediates are returned for inspection.

digest_pipeline runs three stages. extract pulls structured 'name | date | location' lines from the raw text, draft writes a friendly 3-sentence digest from those facts, and polish edits it for concision and warmth under 60 words. All the intermediate results are returned so you can inspect them.
Stage 2 (draft) sees only the extracted facts, not the raw text, and writes a 3-sentence digest.
Stage 3 (polish) sees only the draft and tightens it to under 60 words. The raw announcements are two stages away — this avoids 'lost in the middle'.

route is a classify-then-dispatch router. The router calls llm to classify a ticket as hardware, software, or accounts. A guard defaults unexpected labels to 'software'. Then the specialist for that label answers the ticket.
The router's system prompt demands exactly one word. The guard at line 73 catches any label outside the closed set and silently defaults to 'software' — a code-level fix, not a prompt-level one.

steps.question: What happens when a ticket about a login problem is classified?
steps.answer: The router classifies it as 'accounts', the guard passes, and the accounts specialist returns two concrete steps for account access issues.

The digest pipeline runs. Extract outputs three lines with name, day, and location.
Draft produces a 3-sentence friendly digest mentioning all three events.
Polish shortens it to under 60 words while keeping the key details.
The router processes two tickets. The first (screen flickers) is classified as hardware. The second (cannot log in) is classified as accounts. Each specialist returns two troubleshooting steps.
